narrative: Material PL2__MFFC2B2F exhibits moderate demand variability (CV=43%) with a right-skewed distribution and a slight upward trend of +1.72 units/day over the observation period. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=45%, range 0.19–4.49 days), with transport variability accounting for 72% of lead-time variance. The combined sigma of lead-time demand (908 units) is far larger than the current SAP safety stock of 346 units, making a significant safety stock increase to 1,494 units necessary to achieve the 95% service level target. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with EOQ-derived order quantity of 3,578 units is recommended.
warnings: Optimized policy has HIGHER annual cost than SAP by $1622.94 (29.26%) — higher safety stock drives holding cost increase
Safety lead time differs significantly from SAP: recommended 2.06d vs SAP 3.7d (-1.64 days)

research_insights.selection_rationale: Moderate right-skewed demand with unstable lead times suits a continuous-review reorder-point policy. EOQ balances ordering frequency against holding cost at the given cost parameters. The high sigma_LTD drives a large safety stock, making order quantity optimization the key cost lever.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is non-binding at 38.4% utilization (5,072 / 13,225 units); no capacity constraint modifies the recommended policy.
